title: Native Debugging, Symbols, Sanitizers, and Crash Reports

scout.purpose: Master native debugging, symbols, sanitizers, and crash reports through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend native debugging, symbols, sanitizers, and crash reports.

blocks.text: Native failure evidence includes signal, fault address, registers, threads, memory maps, tombstone, build IDs, and stack addresses. Symbolication requires unstripped symbols that exactly match each ELF binary and ABI; a nearby build can produce plausible but false frames. Preserve release symbols, source revision, NDK, linker, flags, dependencies, mapping, and package version. LLDB supports controlled debugging, while tombstones and ApplicationExitInfo support postmortem analysis.

blocks.text: Use HWASan for intensive test detection where supported, GWP-ASan or MTE for suitable production or test strategies, and ASan only where newer tools are unavailable according to current guidance. UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, fuzzing, CheckJNI, malloc debug, and simpleperf answer different questions. Sanitizers change timing and layout, so reproduce again in a release-like build. Harden with memory-safe languages, bounds, lifetime ownership, PAC/BTI where applicable, and minimal exposed native surface.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Create deterministic native crash fixtures for use-after-free, overflow, abort, and JNI misuse in nonproduction builds. Verify collection, exact symbol upload, symbolication, grouping, privacy, and fix closure for every ABI. Test stripped artifact behavior and missing-symbol alerting. Track native crash-free users by version and device. Do not suppress a crash to keep corrupt state alive. Fix the first causal memory error and add a sanitizer or fuzz regression test.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Symbolicating an arm64 tombstone with symbols from another version or ABI can name the wrong function and misdirect the investigation.

trap_check.mistake: Symbolicating an arm64 tombstone with symbols from another version or ABI can name the wrong function and misdirect the investigation.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Create, capture, symbolicate, and fix a native lifetime crash; verify build IDs, every ABI, HWASan regression, release symbols, and reporting closure.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: What does a native build ID join?
recall.answer: The exact shipped ELF binary and crash addresses to its matching symbol and source artifacts.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
